title: List outcomes and apply the fundamental principle of counting
show: tree or list showing soup choices branching into sandwiches then drinks

example.question:
A cafe lunch deal is one soup, one sandwich and one drink. There are 2 soups, 5 sandwiches and 3 drinks.
(a) How many different deals are there?
(b) The cafe adds one new item to one group. Which group gives the most deals?
example.final: (a) $30$ deals  (b) add a soup, giving $45$ deals

steps.say: Each stage can be chosen in any way, whatever was picked before. So multiply the number of choices at each stage.
Add one to one group at a time and multiply again.
The biggest total wins. State the answer in words.

rows.aside: $\hl{2}{45}$ is the largest, so the cafe should add a **soup**.

title: Construct a sample space for two independent events
show: table/grid of outcomes: H and T against spinner 1 to 4

example.question:
A fair coin is tossed and a fair spinner numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 is spun.
(a) List all the possible outcomes.
(b) Find the probability of a head and an even number.

steps.say: Pair each coin result with each spinner number. Do one row at a time so none are missed.
Look for a head and an even number: the pairs $(H,2)$ and $(H,4)$.
Divide the wanted outcomes by all outcomes.

title: Find a probability with equally likely outcomes
show: 6 by 6 grid of two-dice sums with the sums of 9 or more highlighted

example.question: Two fair dice are thrown and the scores are added. Find the probability that the sum is $9$ or more.

steps.say: Each die has $6$ faces and any face can go with any face. Multiply to get the total number of outcomes.
List the pairs that give a sum of $9$ or more. Count how many pairs give each sum.
Divide the $\hl{1}{10}$ favourable outcomes by the $\hl{2}{36}$ possible outcomes. Cancel to simplest form.

title: Use set notation and Venn diagrams for probability
show: Venn diagram of 40 students: drama only 12, both 6, choir only 8, neither 14

example.question: In a class of $40$ students, $18$ take drama and $14$ take choir. $6$ students take both. A student is picked at random. Find the probability that the student takes neither drama nor choir.

steps.say: Write $\hl{1}{6}$ in the part where the circles overlap. Subtract it from each circle to get the parts with one subject only.
Add the three parts inside the circles. This is everyone who takes at least one subject.
Everyone not in a circle takes neither. Subtract from the total of $40$.
Put the $\hl{2}{14}$ students over the $40$ in the class and cancel.
